about.title: A specialist practice, not a general clinic that also does surgery
body: Bhairavi Dental & Maxillofacial Center was built around a simple gap: most dental clinics in Porur can clean, fill, and extract — but when a case involves impacted wisdom teeth, jaw irregularities, facial trauma, or multiple implants, patients get referred out to a surgical specialist across town.

We are that specialist, in-house. Our oral & maxillofacial surgeon works alongside a general dentist so routine care and complex surgical cases are handled under one roof, with one team that knows your full history.
Every surgical case is explained in plain language before treatment starts — what the procedure involves, what anesthesia is used, and what recovery actually looks like.
highlights: In-house oral & maxillofacial surgeon for complex cases
Wisdom tooth, implant, and jaw surgery under one roof
Clear pre- and post-op guidance for every procedure

services.name: Wisdom Tooth Extraction & Impaction Surgery
services.tagline: Surgical removal of impacted and problem wisdom teeth
services.overview: Impacted wisdom teeth are one of the most common reasons patients are referred to an oral surgeon. We handle the full range in-house, from straightforward extractions to fully impacted teeth requiring surgical removal.
symptoms: Pain or swelling at the back of the jaw
Difficulty opening the mouth fully
Recurring gum infection around the back molars
Crowding or pressure on neighboring teeth
procedure: Clinical exam and X-ray/OPG to assess impaction
Local or sedation anesthesia based on case complexity
Surgical extraction of the impacted tooth
Suturing and post-operative care instructions
benefits: Performed in-house by a qualified oral surgeon
Reduces risk of infection, crowding, and cyst formation
services.recovery: Most patients recover within 5–7 days with mild swelling; a follow-up visit is scheduled for suture removal if needed.

faqs.question: Will I be put to sleep for the extraction?
faqs.answer: Most extractions are done under local anesthesia. Sedation is offered for complex impactions or anxious patients — we'll discuss the right option for your case beforehand.

services.name: Dental Implants
services.tagline: Permanent, natural-feeling replacement for missing teeth
services.overview: We place and restore dental implants for single missing teeth or full-arch cases, combining Dr. Bhairavan's surgical placement with Dr. Suresh's prosthodontic restoration under one treatment plan.
symptoms: One or more missing teeth
Loose or failing dentures
Difficulty chewing due to gaps
procedure: 3D imaging and treatment planning
Surgical placement of the titanium implant
Healing period for osseointegration
Custom crown fitted onto the implant
benefits: Functions and feels like a natural tooth
Prevents bone loss at the missing tooth site
Surgical and restorative work coordinated in-house
services.recovery: Initial healing takes 2–3 weeks; full osseointegration before the final crown typically takes 3–4 months.

services.name: Jaw Surgery (Orthognathic)
services.tagline: Corrective surgery for jaw alignment and bite irregularities
services.overview: Orthognathic surgery corrects significant jaw misalignment that affects bite, breathing, or facial symmetry, usually in coordination with orthodontic treatment before and after surgery.
symptoms: Visible jaw misalignment or facial asymmetry
Chronic difficulty chewing or biting
Jaw pain or TMJ discomfort
Breathing difficulty linked to jaw structure
procedure: Detailed imaging and surgical planning with your orthodontist
Pre-surgical orthodontic preparation where needed
Surgical correction of the jaw under anesthesia
Structured post-operative recovery and follow-up
benefits: Corrects functional bite and breathing issues
Improves facial symmetry and jaw function
Planned jointly with your orthodontist for lasting results
services.recovery: Initial recovery is typically 2–3 weeks, with full healing and bite stabilization over several months.

services.name: Facial Trauma & Reconstruction
services.tagline: Emergency and reconstructive care for facial and jaw injuries
services.overview: We treat fractures and soft tissue injuries to the jaw and face resulting from accidents, falls, or sports injuries, from initial stabilization through reconstructive follow-up.
symptoms: Jaw or facial fracture following an accident
Difficulty closing the mouth or bite misalignment after injury
Facial lacerations near the mouth or jaw
Numbness or swelling after facial trauma
procedure: Emergency clinical assessment and imaging
Stabilization of fractures where required
Surgical repair or reconstruction as needed
Follow-up care through full recovery
services.recovery: Recovery time depends on injury severity; your surgeon will outline a specific timeline after assessment.

services.name: Root Canal Treatment
services.tagline: Save the natural tooth, relieve the pain
services.overview: Root canal treatment removes infected pulp from inside the tooth to eliminate pain and infection while preserving the natural tooth structure.
symptoms: Persistent tooth pain, especially with hot or cold
Swelling or tenderness in the gums
Darkening of the tooth
Pain when chewing or biting
procedure: Diagnosis and X-ray to confirm infection
Removal of infected pulp under local anesthesia
Cleaning and sealing of the root canal
Crown placement to restore the tooth
services.recovery: Mild sensitivity for a few days is normal; most patients return to normal eating within a week.

services.name: General Dental Care
services.tagline: Routine check-ups, cleaning, and preventive care
services.overview: Regular dental check-ups, professional cleaning, fillings, and preventive care to catch issues early and avoid the need for surgical intervention later.
symptoms: Due for a routine check-up or cleaning
Sensitivity or minor cavities
Bleeding or inflamed gums
General dental maintenance
procedure: Comprehensive oral examination
Professional cleaning and scaling
Fillings or minor restorative work as needed
Preventive guidance for ongoing care
benefits: Catches problems before they need surgery
Same team as your surgical specialist if complications arise

faqs.question: Do you accept walk-ins?

faqs.question: What should I expect before a surgical procedure like a wisdom tooth extraction?
faqs.answer: You'll have a consultation with an X-ray or OPG scan first, so your surgeon can explain the procedure, anesthesia option, and recovery timeline before your surgery date is scheduled.

faqs.question: Is anesthesia used for surgical procedures?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most surgical procedures are done under local anesthesia, with sedation options available for more complex cases or anxious patients — this is discussed and agreed on before treatment.

faqs.question: What payment options do you accept?

blogPosts.title: Wisdom Tooth Extraction: What to Expect Before and After
blogPosts.excerpt: A plain-language walkthrough of what happens before, during, and after a wisdom tooth extraction — so there are no surprises on the day.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Arvind Bhairavan
content: Not every wisdom tooth needs to come out — but when one is impacted, causing pain, or putting neighboring teeth at risk, extraction is usually the right call. The first step is always an X-ray or OPG scan to see exactly how the tooth is positioned.

Before the procedure, we walk through the anesthesia option that fits your case. Most extractions use local anesthesia; more complex impactions may call for sedation, which we'll discuss with you well before the surgery date.

The extraction itself is usually done within 30–60 minutes depending on complexity. You'll be given clear aftercare instructions — what to eat, how to manage swelling, and when to avoid rinsing or spitting forcefully.

Mild swelling and discomfort for the first 2–3 days is normal and manageable with prescribed medication. Most patients are back to regular eating within a week, and we schedule a follow-up if sutures need to be removed.
If you're unsure whether your wisdom tooth needs attention, a consultation and scan will give you a clear answer rather than letting the discomfort linger.
